title: Surge Resilience Allocation Plan: tokens/sec & QPS Forecast 2027Q4
summary: Working-capacity worksheet projecting 2027 Q4 peak load by region and mapping to GPU slice requirements. Focus: ensure 30–50% resilience headroom for hosted API critical routes, quantify prewarm and burst pool recommendations, and provide quick reroute/fallback knobs for cross-region coverage.
assumptions:
- Forecast horizon: 2027 Q4 peak week (Black Friday-style surge)
- Average output tokens per request (p99 path): 120 tokens (includes streaming overhead)
- Baseline steady-state measured in Sep 2026 used as "baseline_qps"; projected growth factors applied per region
- Effective tokens/sec capacity per GPU slice: estimated by model class and quantization. Conservative values used: A100-80GB slice = 3,200 tokens/sec; H100-80GB slice = 5,000 tokens/sec (streaming-heavy workloads assumed)
- Safe headroom target expressed as percent of projected_peak capacity (not baseline): default 40% unless noted
- Prewarm latency SLO target: <250ms p95; prewarm pool uses dedicated slices in each region where >10% of global peak originates
- Cross-region failover allowed but incurs 60–120ms added latency and double egress costs
- Fallback to smaller model variants reduces tokens/sec pressure by ~60% per request (quality tradeoff documented elsewhere)

Notes on table calculations: projected_peak_tokens_per_sec = projected_peak_qps * avg_tokens_per_req. required_slices_raw = ceil(projected_peak_tokens_per_sec / tokens_per_slice). required_slices_with_headroom = ceil(required_slices_raw * (1 + headroom_pct/100)). suggested_prewarm_slices is rounded to nearest whole slice and biased up for regions with historically spiky patterns.
computational_notes:
- We used conservative slice throughput numbers derived from bench runs on a mixture of medium-length conversations and streaming outputs (median sequence 120 tokens). Actual tokens/sec will vary by model family and sequence length distribution.
- For H100 estimations we used 5k tps/slice; for A100 we used 3.2k tps/slice. If we can enable quantization pattern Q4-2027 these can improve by ~20% and reduce required slices accordingly.
- Network and ingress pods assumed to be horizontally scaled and not the bottleneck; if ingress CPU is constrained, effective tokens/sec per slice can drop by 10–25% — see sensitivity section.
- When projecting slices we intentionally round up to avoid fractional slices; we also prefer whole-GPU assignments for Dedicated customers unless virtualization (multi-tenant slices) is available.
sensitivity_analysis:
Scenario A: avg_tokens drops to 90 (lighter prompts) -> global projected tokens/sec reduces ~25% -> required slices drop by ~25% and headroom buffer becomes larger.
Scenario B: effective tokens/slice -10% due to CPU/network -> required slices increase by ~12% (ceil effects can make this +1 slice in small regions).
Scenario C: simultaneous regional surge (us-west + eu-west at 120% of local peak) -> global peak shift requires ability to shift 6–8 slices cross-region; recommend keep cold pool of 10% global capacity for cross-region warm-up.
Sensitivity recommendation: maintain a small global burst pool equivalent to 8% of total required_slices_with_headroom to cover unexpected concentration events.

risk_and_mitigations:
- Risk: over-provisioning increases monthly committed costs. Mitigation: use mix of reserved + on-demand burst pools and optimize by model-targeted quantization.
- Risk: cross-region failover impacts latency-sensitive customers. Mitigation: define SLAs per route and use routing policy to prefer local region; fallback only when route-level SLOs remain acceptable.
- Risk: bench numbers are stale when new model variants are onboarded. Mitigation: gate model rollouts via canary with tokens/sec measurement and auto-roll back if capacity metrics exceed thresholds.
